title: Adaptive Test-Time Semantic Debiasing for AI-Generated Image Detection

rationale: CSAIID is a separately stated contribution with COCO/PartiPrompts provenance, three generator models, semantic curation and fixed balanced category subsets (R1). The six-category resource and comparative cross-semantic protocol grouped by external training source substantively evaluate detectors beyond ordinary experiments (R2).

R1.reason: p2 explicitly identifies CSAIID among contributions; §4 p5 documents provenance, caption/prompt generation, category curation and count; p1 links public dataset.

R2.reason: CSAIID is expressly designed to assess cross-semantic generalization (p2), with fixed six semantic test subsets, external-training-source groups and ACC comparison rules (§5.2 pp5–6, Table 1 p6). This is a reusable evaluation resource, not merely many model results.

scientific_review.empirical_validity: Numbers are reported, not reproduced; generator/source/semantic shifts are intertwined. No guarantee of semantically disjoint training/test object inventories established.
scientific_review.causal_interpretation: LSUN-to-ImageNet comparisons also alter forgery generators/training distributions; Table 1 discussion p6 acknowledges generator influence. Accuracy changes cannot isolate semantic diversity as a causal effect.
scientific_review.availability: p1 public-data hyperlink resolves in cached annotation inventory to a Google Drive file; not visited or downloaded during recovery, and license/access status not verified.
scientific_review.reproducibility: Fixed category sizes and training/evaluation conventions documented, but exact seeds, per-generator integer category counts and dataset manifest not recovered; no separate CSAIID training/validation split asserted.

evidence.claim: Named cross-semantic resource is curated from COCO real images and caption-conditioned fakes, with additional PartiPrompts fictional/abstract/world-knowledge content. Real counterparts for unpaired prompts are category-matched COCO training images, not matched scenes.

Six categories: Outdoor Scenes, People, Animals, Vehicles, Food, Complex. Synthetic generators are Stable Diffusion v2, LDM and LCM; paper claims 1:1:1 generator balance. Complex captures difficult multi-concept/uncategorizable scenes.

evidence.locator: §5.1/5.2 p5; Table 1 caption and discussion p6
evidence.claim: External training comes from UniForen (LSUN/ProGAN) or GenImage (ImageNet/SD1.4); ACC is reported per semantic subset. Official weights are used for previous methods; starred NPR results use reimplemented training with official code. NoDown-S and DIRE are explicit same-training-set exceptions. DF3 is the validation resource for ATTSD settings, not CSAIID.

quantitative_evidence.caveat: 1,000 synthetic images per subset is not divisible by three; exact per-generator integer counts/rounding are absent. Do not invent equal integer counts.

quantitative_evidence.reported: ATTSD average ACC 82.30% for LSUN/ProGAN training, 90.42% for ImageNet/SD1.4; NPR 71.33% and 84.02%, respectively.
quantitative_evidence.caveat: Paired training settings change both real-source semantics and fake generator; the 8.12-point ATTSD difference does not isolate a semantic causal effect.

quantitative_evidence.reported: DF3 selected for validation; test batch size 1 with six adaptation gradient steps per sample.
quantitative_evidence.caveat: Test-time adaptation incurs additional computation and uses target inputs; does not establish a static single-pass or label-free-reproduction guarantee.

limitations: Source confirms reusable cross-semantic evaluation contribution; category overlap with existing training concepts and multi-generator changes limit claims of controlled pure semantic shift.
No fetched dataset, license, manifest, duplicate audit or experiment reproduction.
Fixed evaluation subsets are documented; no dedicated CSAIID training/validation/test partition is claimed.
Paper author/DOI/workshop identity retained without publication metadata edits.
confidence: High for bounded R1/R2 contribution support; empirical causal and operational reproducibility limits remain.
